item.title: My Poor Kitty
item.description:
My 15 year old Tortoiseshell "Shelly" escaped from the house last Monday morning, and when we finally found her late in the evening she was not usher left hind leg. We rushed her to the emergency vet to get checked out and they found that her upper femur was shattered.
She weirdly was not in much pain, she just wanted to eat and play like normal. But they zooted her up on the good drugs to be sure she was comfortable.
Sadly, they said our only option was amputation. Shelly is over 15 years old, and we were so worried this would be too much for her to handle.
All the vet staff were impressed with Shelly's great attitude, she loves everyone. The whole time she wanted cuddles and belly rubs. While getting assessed, they discovered she had a terrible UTI that showed no symptoms at all. It came up in her blood work and urinalysis. She was just days away from getting really sick. So we were able to start nipping that in the bud.
Nicole (nicnak044) Forbidden lottery numbers 4 5 4 6 2 5 3
Fresh out of surgery as a tripod. Her tail was wrapped to keep it clean. She's on strong pain killers and antibiotics for the next 10 days.
I was so afraid the first few days as she would not eat or drink.
But as of yesterday she is eating and drinking and going on short walks around the house with me! She's using the litter box and acting very normal! We have a cone for her but she has no interest in touching her stitches at all so far!
I have her in a crate to make sure she rests and the other cats don't bother her, so far they only want to comfort her. I set up a camera to keep an eye on here and make sure she is kept safe. This entire ordeal cost us close to $7000, we don't have $7000... So times are going to be very tough for a while. (well, tougher, as it's already been pretty bad lately)

item.title: GovBrief Today #582
item.description: Police in Arlington, Virginia, opened a criminal investigation of ICE agents this week for a beating the federal government calls "necessary force." José Mejía Hernandez was walking to a bus stop one morning last month when two men in plain clothes got out of an unmarked car. He ran. He says he remembers a jolt from a stun gun and then waking up at George Washington University Hospital, where doctors found bleeding inside his skull. His lawyers gave police bystander video and statements from witnesses who saw an officer's vehicle hit him. ICE strapped an ankle monitor on him and let him go. Homeland Security says a man whose only conviction is for public intoxication in 2020 went to the hospital "out of precaution." His lawyers released photos showing both eyes blackened and one side of his face scraped raw from cheekbone to lip. Virginia's attorney general said he would not look at the case without a police report. Nobody in government had filed one. 17 days after his arrest, Mejía Hernandez did. item.description: Wile E. Coyote is getting his comeback after all Coyote vs. Acme is actually expanding for its second weekend, moving into 3,727 North American theaters compared with 3,575 during its opening weekend. And considering what happened behind the scenes, that's pretty wild. The movie opened at No. 2 domestically with $15.9 million, giving distributor Ketchup Entertainment its biggest opening ever. Even crazier? This is the same movie Warner Bros. once planned to shelve completely. Instead of disappearing into a vault, Coyote vs. Acme is now getting a real theatrical run - and audiences have the chance to decide what happens next. So if you've been waiting years to see Wile E. Coyote finally get his moment on the big screen... this is your chance.
